references.text: The Ten Commandments begin with the command to fear and serve the Lord alone, forbidding the worship of other gods, which is central to Joshua's exhortation.
Moses commands Israel to fear the Lord and serve him alone, the same fundamental command that Joshua gives to the people.
Moses asks what the Lord requires of Israel: to fear him, walk in his ways, love him, and serve him with all their heart.
The command to follow the Lord, fear him, keep his commands, obey his voice, and serve him - the same themes found in Joshua 24:14.
Samuel exhorts Israel to turn to the Lord with all their heart and remove foreign gods, paralleling Joshua's exhortation.
Samuel urges the people to fear the Lord and serve him faithfully with all their heart, the same message that Joshua conveys.
Ezekiel describes how the ancestors of the Israelites worshiped idols in Egypt, as referenced by Joshua.
An exhortation to serve God in a way that pleases him, with reverence and godly fear, in line with Joshua's call to serve the Lord.
Jesus says that those who worship God must worship him in spirit and truth, which corresponds with Joshua's call to serve the Lord in sincerity and truth.
